subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Pascal's Principle: Pressure Everywhere
description: A micro-lesson that makes Pascal's Principle: Pressure Everywhere usable.

hook.text: Press on a sealed fluid and the pressure spreads equally in every direction. Pascal discovered this in 1653.

buildup.text: Pressure applied at one point transmits undiminished to every point in the fluid and to the container walls.

discovery.text: A small piston pressing hard on fluid creates the same pressure at a large piston. Force multiplies by area ratio.

twist.text: You gain force but lose distance. Push the small piston ten centimeters and the large one moves one centimeter.

climax.text: Every hydraulic jack, car brake, and excavator arm runs on Pascal's principle. One idea, endless machines.

punchline.text: Pressure doesn't play favorites. It pushes on everything equally.

quiz.question: What does Pascal's principle state about pressure in a confined fluid?
options: Pressure decreases with distance from the point of application
Pressure transmits equally and undiminished in all directions
Pressure only acts downward due to gravity
